required_coverage.description: Open site (GET /) -> heading 'Mnemonic Protocol' visible -> click 'Start chat' -> chat page shown -> fill message input -> click Send (or Enter) -> mock POST /chat to return {response: 'answer text'} -> assert bot message 'answer text' appears in log -> click download link -> assert response Content-Disposition or file download initiated
required_coverage.mock_strategy: page.route('/chat', ...) to return deterministic JSON; page.route('/download-knowledge', ...) to return a minimal zip buffer

required_coverage.description: On chat page, mock POST /chat to return {response: 'I can only answer questions about the Mnemonic Protocol.'} -> send an off-topic message -> assert rejection text visible in message log
required_coverage.mock_strategy: page.route('/chat', handler that returns the rejection text) -- must be deterministic, no live Ollama
required_coverage.note: Rejection wording must match whatever the backend prompt instructs. Use a plausible rejection string and assert it appears.

required_coverage.description: Navigate to chat page, inject messageCount = 49 into React component state via page.evaluate() or by using window.__setMessageCount if exposed, OR send 1 message via mocked /chat which increments counter to 50 -- then assert: (1) 'Session limit reached' banner appears (role=alert), (2) textarea is disabled, (3) Send button is disabled, (4) textarea placeholder reads 'Session limit reached.'
required_coverage.mock_strategy: page.route('/chat', ...) to return a valid response for the 50th message. Counter starts at 49 (injected or pre-loaded via 49 mocked round-trips at minimum). The spec says 'inject counter state at 49' -- preferred approach is React state injection via evaluate() or exposing a test hook.
required_coverage.note: Do NOT do 50 real round-trips. The point of this test is fast counter injection. If React state cannot be injected via evaluate(), use 49 mocked route responses to pre-warm the counter, then assert limit on the 50th response.

required_coverage.description: On chat page, mock POST /chat to return HTTP 503 with body {error: 'Service temporarily unavailable.', code: 'service_unavailable'} for all attempts (to exhaust retries) -> send message -> assert error message 'Service temporarily unavailable. Try again later.' appears in message log with error styling (border-error class or role=alert on message)
required_coverage.mock_strategy: page.route('/chat', route => route.fulfill({status: 503, json: {error: '...', code: 'service_unavailable'}})) -- must be stable for 3 retry attempts
required_coverage.note: The api.ts client retries 3x on 503. The mock must respond with 503 on all 3 attempts. This is naturally handled by a persistent page.route() handler. Do NOT use arbitrary timeouts to simulate Ollama being down.

playwright_best_practices.requirement: All network calls must be mocked via page.route(). No live backend dependency in E2E tests.
playwright_best_practices.reason: Test determinism. Live Ollama is non-deterministic and unavailable in CI.

playwright_best_practices.requirement: Use semantic selectors: getByRole(), getByLabel(), getByText(). Avoid CSS class selectors or XPath.
playwright_best_practices.reason: Class names (bg-accent-primary, etc.) are implementation details and change with styling refactors.

playwright_best_practices.requirement: Use expect(locator).toBeVisible() and expect(locator).toBeDisabled() -- not manual waitFor(). Playwright auto-waits.
playwright_best_practices.reason: Manual waitFor with fixed timeouts creates flaky tests.

playwright_best_practices.requirement: Each test must use beforeEach to set up routes and navigate. Tests must be fully isolated.
playwright_best_practices.reason: fullyParallel: true in playwright.config.ts requires each test to be independent.

playwright_best_practices.requirement: The error state test must account for retry delay (api.ts retries 3x with 1s, 2s backoff). Either mock timers via page.clock.install() or set a sufficient test timeout (>=10s).
playwright_best_practices.reason: Without mocked clocks or sufficient timeout, the test will time out waiting for all retries to complete.

test_isolation_notes: App.tsx uses in-memory React state (useState). Page refresh resets all state. Each test that needs a fresh counter should navigate fresh.
Session ID is generated with crypto.randomUUID() on mount. No server-side state means tests are inherently isolated from each other.
The session limit counter injection is the trickiest isolation point -- document clearly how the initial counter value is set.
